I'm 74 this year, and I've been working these 5 mu for 54 years — longer than most folks in the village have been alive. It's just me and my wife now. Our children left for the city years ago. My bones ache in the morning, but the land doesn't wait.

I keep 4 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 1 mu in cotton. I used to grow more cotton, but at my age, bending down to pick it three or four times a year is hard on my back. Still, cotton brings in cash, and we need cash for my wife's blood pressure medicine and for when the pump breaks. So I keep that 1 mu.

**The wheat** is already in the ground from last October. I put down base fertilizer before winter — about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, same as I've done for decades. Now it's April and the wheat is at jointing. I need to topdress soon. The extension agent says I should put more, but fertilizer prices went up again this year. Old Wang down the lane skipped his topdress two years ago to save money and his yield dropped by almost a third — I remember it clear as day. I'm scared of that. I'll put about 8 kg of urea per mu at topdressing. It's less than the rich farms use, but it's what I can afford without emptying my pocket. I'll irrigate twice more before harvest in early June if the rain doesn't come. Pumping water costs electricity money, so I watch the sky every morning. I'm hoping for about 360 kg per mu — same as last year, God willing.

**Cotton** — I'm planting that 1 mu right now, mid-April. I plowed it myself with the small walking tractor I bought fifteen years ago. I put fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about one bag of compound fertilizer for the whole mu. I buy improved cotton seed every year — 40 yuan per mu — because saved cotton seed doesn't grow right. Cotton needs spraying for bollworms and aphids, maybe three or four times this summer. I do the spraying myself with the backpack sprayer. Harvest is September through October, picking three or four times. My wife helps, but if the bolls open all at once we might be in trouble. I expect about 210 kg of lint per mu if the bugs don't get bad.

**Maize** — I need to buy the hybrid seed now so I'm ready when the wheat comes off in early June. The window is tight, maybe five or six days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire the neighbor's tractor to plow quick after the combine goes through — costs me about 80 yuan for the 4 mu. I plant the hybrid seed right away. For fertilizer, I put down compound at planting, about 12-13 kg nitrogen worth per mu total. If the plants look yellow when they're knee-high, I'll topdress a little urea, but usually the base is enough. One or two irrigations for the maize, depending on the rains. I should get about 410 kg per mu if the autumn drought doesn't hit.

I thought about buying more fertilizer for all the crops, but I need to keep 500 yuan in my pocket for emergencies. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps — that's what 54 years has taught me. Better to sleep with a little cash under the mattress than to gamble everything on the crops.
